I mean, I can remember grade school teachers saying I was smart — like, “she understands it when she pays attention,” that kind of thing — but I was always losing papers or leaving them in my desk, or missing part of the directions.\n\nAnd they’d have to remind me to finish classwork. I’d start it, then somehow get off track, and then everyone else would be turning theirs in and I’d be like, wait, what are we doing? I used to think that was just me being messy, honestly. My backpack was a disaster too, but—sorry, that’s probably not the point. It was happening way before this job, yeah.\n\nDoctor: Outside of work, do you also have this same kind of trouble remembering and following through in your day-to-day life?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I mean… outside work too, but honestly the work stuff is the biggest mess right now. Like the callbacks and work orders and all those little “I’ll get back to you” things — I say them like I’m going to remember, and then they just pile up.\n\nAt home it’s more like the same pattern, I guess, but work is where it’s really catching up to me because there are actual consequences. They sent me here because they’re worried I’m going to blow my chance to move up, which is… frustrating, because I really am trying.\n\nDoctor: Do you often find your mind drifting when someone is talking to you, even when you want to pay attention?\n\nPatient: Yeah… yes, that happens a lot. Like my supervisor will be talking right to me about a repair or an audit thing, and I’m looking at him, nodding, trying to listen. But then only the first part really sticks, and by the time he’s on the next part I’m kind of… not gone exactly, but it’s not landing.\n\nThen I have to ask him to repeat it, which is embarrassing because I was literally staring at him. I don’t know if I’d call it that. I’m not sure that’s the same thing you mean. I don’t really have a clear answer on that one.\n\nDoctor: In conversations with family or friends, do you also lose track of what the other person is saying?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I mean… with family or friends it can happen, but the clearest example is honestly at work. So I have to start over, which is frustrating because I was right there doing it.\n\nDoctor: Do you spend a lot of time worrying, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?\n\nPatient: Um… worrying? I don’t know. I’m not sure. I don’t really think of myself as sitting around worrying all the time. I’d have to pay more attention to that, I guess.\n\nDoctor: Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?\n\nPatient: Um… down or depressed? I don’t know. I wouldn’t say depressed, I guess. I’m not sure. I haven’t really been tracking it like that. Then there was this safety review that ended up on my record, which… I keep thinking about that. I was working toward moving up, you know, and now I’m scared this is going to ruin that path.\n\nSo yeah, it causes trouble at home because I’m carrying it around with me, but the serious part right now is work.\n\nDoctor: At home, do you often forget everyday tasks like paying bills, appointments, or returning messages?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I mean… at home, yes, but the thing that’s really gotten bad is callbacks and work orders. I’ll tell someone, “Yeah, I’ll follow up with you,” and then it just—unless it’s right in front of me, it disappears.\n\nAnd then I’ll remember later, like while I’m making dinner or looking for my keys, and I think, okay, I need to call them back, but then something else happens and it’s gone again. It’s not even just messages, it’s scheduled callbacks, basic follow-ups I promised people… and now it’s piled up.\n\nThat’s kind of what brought me in, honestly. Work sent me here because it’s getting to the point where I’m scared I’m going to lose my chance at moving up.\n\nDoctor: At home, do you also leave chores or other everyday tasks unfinished because you get distracted?\n\nPatient: Yeah… I mean, chores, sure, but it’s the same pattern I have at work, honestly. Like I won’t close out the ticket, or I’ll forget to label the panel, or I’m supposed to check back with the tenant and make sure it’s all okay, and I just move on because someone else is asking me something or I notice another problem.\n\nAnd then later it looks like I didn’t finish the job, even though in my head I did the hard part already. That’s the part that gets me in trouble.\n\nDoctor: When you forget something, does it usually come back to you later once you get a reminder or see the situation again?\n\nPatient: Yeah, sometimes it comes back when I see it again, like if the work order is sitting there or somebody calls again and I’m like, oh God, I was supposed to call you back.\n\nBut that’s kind of the problem—it comes back after it’s already piled up. What brought me in is I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks and work orders and even basic follow-ups I promised people.
